svg.title: redisq wake-ups: an enqueue wakes a random idle consumer, and a once-a-second nudge catches the wakes that land on a busy one
svg.desc: Two consumers, C1 and C2, each a DistributedQueue with a varmq worker running one job at a time, wait on one Redis list. At the start the queue is empty, both consumers are free, and both are members of the :idle set, which Subscribe joined them to. Every consumer runs a nudge once a second: when the queue is empty it adds itself to :idle (SADD), and when items wait it removes itself (SREM) and pokes its own worker. Job X is enqueued: one script pushes it (RPUSH) and wakes one idle consumer, because one item waits. SPOP takes a random member of :idle, here C1, and PUBLISH sends the wake on C1's own channel. C1 is free, so it pops X at once and runs it. C1's next nudge finds the queue empty and puts C1 back in :idle although C1 is busy. Job Y is enqueued: SPOP takes C1 again, the PUBLISH reaches C1, and C1 ignores it because it is busy; its own nudge a moment later pokes it and is ignored too. Y waits, and C2 is still in :idle. Less than a second later C2's nudge finds Y waiting: it removes C2 from :idle and pokes C2, which pops Y. C1 finishes X; its Len() call finds the queue empty and puts it back in :idle. C2's next nudge, with the queue empty, puts C2 back in :idle while it still runs Y, and C2 then finishes Y. At the end the queue is empty, both consumers are free, and both are in :idle. Each job was popped once. Redis round trips are slowed down; the nudge period is the real one second.

g.text: nudge: each consumer, once a second

svg.text: times not to scale: round trips slowed down
SPOP is random; this run draws C1 both times
n = items waiting after the push
